questions.q: Against whom did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to speak?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to speak against the sanctuaries; against the land of Israel.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say he would cut off from the land of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would cut off both the righteous people and the wicked people from the land of Israel.

questions.q: Against whom would Yahweh send his sword, from the south to the north?
questions.a: Yahweh would send his sword against all people in the land, both righteous and wicked, from the south to the north.

questions.q: What would everyone know after Yahweh brought out his sword?
questions.a: Everyone would know that Yahweh himself had brought out his sword, and it would not return again.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do before the eyes of the people?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to groan before the eyes of the people.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to act this way before the eyes of the people?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to act this way to show what it would be like for them when Yahweh brought the sword against them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to prophesy about?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to prophesy about a sword that was sharpened and polished for slaughter, even against the royal scepter of his son.

questions.q: Who was the sharpened and polished sword to be given to?
questions.a: The polished and sharpened sword was to be given into the hand of a killer.

questions.q: On whom would that sword come?
questions.a: That sword would come on Yahweh’s people and the leaders of Israel.

questions.q: What did the Lord Yahweh say the sword would do to the scepter that rejected him?
questions.a: The Lord Yahweh said the sword would destroy the royal power of Judah, which rejected his warnings.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with his hands, and what would the sword do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to clap his hands together, and he said the sword would kill many people, striking them again and again from every side.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh station soldiers with pointed swords?
questions.a: Yahweh stationed soldiers with pointed swords at every city gate.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command the soldiers with the sword to do, to the right and to the left?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded the soldiers to slash their swords to the right and to the left, wherever they were directed.

questions.q: What would come to rest after the great slaughter?
questions.a: After the great slaughter, Yahweh’s fury would come to rest.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to set out for the army of the king of Babylon?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to set out two roads for the army of the king of Babylon to travel.

questions.q: What were the destinations of the two roads assigned for the king of Babylon?
questions.a: The two destinations were Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Judah and Jerusalem.

questions.q: How would the king of Babylon determine which road to take?
questions.a: The king of Babylon would obtain a prophetic message from divination to determine which road to take.

questions.q: What did the divination for Jerusalem tell the king of Babylon to do?
questions.a: The divination told the king of Babylon to set battering rams against the gates, shout the battle cry, build a siege ramp, and build siege walls against Jerusalem.

questions.q: Of what would the king of Babylon accuse Israel in order to attack them?
questions.a: The king of Babylon would accuse Israel of violating their sworn oath in order to attack them.

questions.q: What did the Lord Yahweh say would happen to Israel because of their remembered sins?
questions.a: The Lord Yahweh said Israel’s enemies would seize them because of their remembered sins.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the wicked ruler of Israel to do, and why?
questions.a: Yahweh told the wicked ruler of Israel to remove his turban and crown, because he was about to turn everything upside down and leave Jerusalem in ruins until the rightful ruler comes.

questions.q: When did Yahweh say he would restore the crown in Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would restore the crown in Israel when one came who had a right to it.

questions.q: What do the prophets of Ammon do for the people of Ammon?
questions.a: Ammon’s prophets see empty visions for the people of Ammon, while they perform rituals to come up with lies for the people of Ammon.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh say he would judge the people of Ammon?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would judge the people of Ammon in the land of their origin, the place where they were created.

questions.q: Who was the Lord Yahweh going to give the people of Ammon over to?
questions.a: The Lord Yahweh was going to give the Ammonites into the hand of brutish men, craftsmen of destruction.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the people of Ammon in the end?
questions.a: Yahweh said fire would destroy them, they would die in their own land, and no one would remember them again.

commentary.text: The ruin of Judah under the emblem of a sharp sword. (Ezek. 21:1-17) The approach of the king of Babylon described. (Ezek. 21:18-27) The destruction of the Ammonites. (Ezek. 21:28-32)

Ezek. 21:1-17 Here is an explanation of the parable in the last chapter. It is declared that the Lord was about to cut off Jerusalem and the whole land, that all might know it was his decree against a wicked and rebellious people. It behoves those who denounce the awful wrath of God against sinners, to show that they do not desire the woful day. The example of Christ teaches us to lament over those whose ruin we declare. Whatever instruments God uses in executing his judgments, he will strengthen them according to the service they are employed in. The sword glitters to the terror of those against whom it is drawn. It is a sword to others, a rod to the people of the Lord. God is in earnest in pronouncing this sentence, and the prophet must show himself in earnest in publishing it.

Ezek. 21:18-27 By the Spirit of prophecy Ezekiel foresaw Nebuchadnezzar's march from Babylon, which he would determine by divination. The Lord would overturn the government of Judah, till the coming of Him whose right it is. This seems to foretell the overturnings of the Jewish nation to the present day, and the troubles of states and kingdoms, which shall make way for establishing the Messiah's kingdom throughout the earth. The Lord secretly leads all to adopt his wise designs. And in the midst of the most tremendous warnings of wrath, we still hear of mercy, and some mention of Him through whom mercy is shown to sinful men.

Ezek. 21:28-32 The diviners of the Ammonites made false prophecies of victory. They would never recover their power, but in time would be wholly forgotten. Let us be thankful to be employed as instruments of mercy; let us use our understandings in doing good; and let us stand aloof from men who are only skilful to destroy.
